keyVerseText: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
rootMeaning: The word μεγαλωσύνη (megalōsýnē) derives from the root μέγας (mégas), which conveys the idea of greatness or largeness in a broad sense, including strength and majesty. This root emphasizes not just size but also the quality of being exalted or mighty. Thus, μεγαλωσύνη carries a sense of majesty that is deeply connected to an overwhelming greatness or divine grandeur, going beyond a mere title to express an inherent, powerful dignity.
usageInScripture: The term μεγαλωσύνη appears three times in Scripture and is consistently translated as 'majesty' or 'of the Majesty,' highlighting its association with divine grandeur. The majority of occurrences emphasize the majestic nature of God or His presence, indicating that the word is reserved for describing the supreme greatness attributed to the divine. This consistent usage underscores the word's theological weight and its function in portraying God’s exalted status.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding μεγαλωσύνη as majesty rooted in greatness enriches our grasp of God's nature as supremely exalted and powerful. It reveals that God's majesty is not superficial but grounded in His overwhelming greatness and authority, affirming His divinity. This term invites believers to approach God with awe and reverence, recognizing His sovereign rule and divine glory. It also highlights Christ's divine identity, who, as the radiance of God's glory, shares in this majesty, affirming the unity and supremacy of the Godhead. Thus, μεγαλωσύνη anchors Christian worship and faith in the reality of God's majestic and mighty presence.
keyVerseReflection: Hebrews 1:3 describes Christ as seated at the right hand of the 'Majesty on high,' using μεγαλωσύνη to convey the supreme divine authority and glory of God the Father. This word enriches the verse by emphasizing that Christ’s position is not merely honorific but is at the very throne of God's majestic and exalted nature. It underscores the intimate relationship between Christ and the divine Majesty, affirming His role in upholding all things by divine power and His participation in the divine glory.
